notes: Three expected shared-prior misreads. (1) DEFENSIVE-KIT-INERT prior: every line here is heal/shield/HP, and the lazy model skips them all as 'no damage' — but taxonomy #4 applies with force: controlComp contains CROWN, whose on-recovery trigger is driven by snow-crane's every-3-charges heal and burst heal, so heal EVENT cadence is directly damage-bearing; the tests must be tandem tests through crown's buffApply log, not totals-only. (2) The Proof-of-Violation → Terminated Contract state machine is a real mid-fight CASCADE (external heals → 3 stacks → S1 grant + Exclusive Recovery Agreement drop team-wide → S2a heal goes dead → crown procs stop), and the source gate ('recovery NOT from this unit') is load-bearing: counting self-heals flips the cascade in every comp; a correct model keeps it dormant in healer-less comps. controlComp's liter and helm both emit heals, so the cascade is live in the standard fixture — the driver needs BOTH an external-healer assertion and a no-external-healer control. (3) FIXTURE HAZARD: snow-crane is Burst II — controlComp(carry) seats the carry at B3 with crown fixed at B2, so as authored she'd compete with crown under first-ready selection (or never cast if crown wins). The burstCast-keyed lines (burst heal, gainPierce) and their vs-fullBurstEnter distinguishers depend on her actually casting some but not necessarily all rotations — the test fixture must establish her real cast pattern (or patch the comp) before asserting counts. Also verify the shield line stays fullBurstEnter (fires every FB) while the burst heal stays burstCast — the kit deliberately splits these two trigger identities and a uniform keying either way is wrong on exactly one of them. Engine-primitive note: ally-side statuses (Exclusive Recovery Agreement / Terminated Contract / Proof of Violation) have no first-class channel (targetStatus is enemy-only) — expect a resource-pool approximation; the review should accept any encoding that reproduces the event-log behavior asserted above and reject encodings that hardcode the cascade as never/always-on.
